title: A declined hook advances to its failure state
situation: A scheduled adventure hook was available, but the players appeared tired and might skip it.
noticed: Player energy/availability mattered more than forcing the day's prepared content.
intervention: Brendon explicitly told the group they did not have to adventure and noted that he already had a fail condition for leaving the situation unchecked.
observed_result: Players immediately volunteered to go; the hook remained voluntary, while the world consequence remained credible.
reusable_judgment: Make participation optional while keeping the situation consequential. A hook can be declined; the world does not freeze when it is.
representative_line: “we don't have to have an adventure. I have a fail condition for not checking it out”

title: Recover momentum by reconnecting an existing unresolved thread
situation: Play had drifted and the group asked what was on the agenda.
noticed: The game needed direction, but an existing Chinnokin thread was already alive in the fiction.
intervention: Brendon chose the Chinnokin storyline as the fastest way back toward planned content, then pointed to the in-world visitor at Fathoms Bridge instead of inventing a new quest.
observed_result: Players immediately recognized the thread and began discussing how to pursue it.
reusable_judgment: When play drifts, steer first through an unresolved thread already present in the world. Prefer reconnection over replacement.
representative_line: “The quickest way to get us back onto story is to pick up the chinnokin storyline”

title: Prepared combat is subordinate to current party state
situation: Four players were available late in the final week, with mixed resource depletion, and a preplanned fight was ready.
noticed: The planned encounter assumptions no longer matched the actual party state and available time.
intervention: Brendon declined to default into the preplanned fight and instead considered a mostly-RP version or mobs rather than bosses, explicitly asking whether that would be satisfying.
observed_result: The group discussed what kind of play would feel worthwhile rather than being pushed into the scheduled boss structure.
reusable_judgment: Re-evaluate prepared encounters at the moment of delivery. Preserve the intended experience, not the mere fact that an encounter was prepared.
representative_line: “So 4 at depleted resources. My gut says don't take you into the preplanned fight.”

title: Handwave mechanics when the meaningful outcome is already chosen
situation: A player had deliberately asked for a dramatic limb loss, and another player asked whether healing mechanics were still necessary afterward.
noticed: The central dramatic outcome was consensual and already achieved; extra resolution risked becoming procedural noise.
values: player intent, dramatic payoff, mechanical relevance.
intervention: Brendon allowed the bleeding to be stopped if desired but was willing to handwave the remainder because the scene had delivered the requested outcome.
observed_result: The table treated the result as a successful dramatic moment rather than reopening it through unnecessary rolls.
reusable_judgment: Use mechanics for uncertainty, resistance, cost, or consequences. Do not use them ceremonially after all relevant participants have intentionally chosen the core outcome.
representative_line: “im willing to hand wave because your helping a player who asked to loose a limb in glorious fashion”

title: Do not handwave away a question that has become character arc
situation: A Golden Dawn character wanted painful memories removed; players asked whether the required magic could simply be handwaved.
noticed: The request touched faction allegiance, memory, betrayal, and future identity—material with strong downstream story value.
values: character continuity, faction through-line, player agency, future payoff.
intervention: Brendon refused to handwave the question, called it a good arc, then narrowed the effect: the trial could be forgotten without erasing the character's allegiance; if the player still wanted to leave, that choice could be roleplayed for another reason.
observed_result: The conversation shifted from bypassing the problem to defining what the character actually wanted to forget and what consequences would remain.
reusable_judgment: When a shortcut would erase an emerging character problem with future story value, slow down and preserve the choice-bearing part of the problem.
representative_line: “I won't hand wave. this is good arc”

title: Compress low-value transit when time becomes the scarce resource
situation: A scene had reached the point where the party only needed to return to town, while real-world session time was running short.
noticed: The trip no longer promised a meaningful choice or payoff proportional to the time it would consume.
intervention: Brendon handwaved the trip back to town specifically for time concerns.
observed_result: Players immediately agreed and play moved on.
reusable_judgment: Skip transitions once their remaining play value is lower than the time they consume. Persistent worlds do not require simulating every minute.
representative_line: “I'm willing to hand wave the trip back to town at this point for time concerns.”

title: Let players choose the granularity of low-stakes play
situation: A player wanted routine healing potions while Brendon had only a few minutes available.
noticed: The transaction mattered to inventory, but the player might or might not value the shopping interaction itself.
intervention: Brendon offered a fast handwaved purchase at listed prices now, or a full shopping interaction later.
observed_result: The player chose the simple transaction and got the items without consuming a full scene.
reusable_judgment: For low-stakes procedures, offer resolution at the level of detail the player actually values. Do not confuse simulation detail with roleplay quality.
representative_line: “if you know the prices I can hand wave a little shopping... If you want a shopping trip interaction... later”

title: Promote emergent player material into bespoke future content
situation: Early play was generating side relationships and situations beyond the written daily events.
noticed: Some unplanned material had enough story energy to justify additional DM attention.
intervention: Brendon first said he was considering improv sessions for things that caught his eye story-wise, then formalized DM invitationals as short one-shots initiated by players or DMs to tell unplanned stories created cooperatively.
observed_result: The campaign gained an explicit mechanism for converting emergent play into prepared spotlight scenes.
reusable_judgment: Watch for player-created details that imply more story than they currently contain. Promote the strongest into future scenes instead of trying to pre-author every worthwhile thread.
representative_line: “improv sessions if I find things that catch my eye story wise”

title: Reduce authored density as campaign history becomes richer
situation: The written document still contained a day-by-day Week 5 spine, but four weeks of actual play had produced player priorities, unfinished business, and invitationals.
noticed: Accumulated live history had become a better source of relevant content than filling every remaining day with fixed authored material.
intervention: Brendon asked players to DM what they wanted to explore or accomplish and stated that Week 5 was deliberately less written so players could lead and DMs could accommodate more invitationals, while retaining selected major fights.
observed_result: Players were later given a menu of outstanding goals and asked to set priorities rather than being marched through a complete fixed schedule.
reusable_judgment: Front-load structure when campaign history is thin. As meaningful history accumulates, leave increasing prep capacity available to answer what actually happened.
representative_line: “The game is far less written in week 5 to let the players lead more”

title: Use collective attention to select which pressure becomes foreground
situation: Roanoke contained simultaneous internal political problems and external threats, and Brendon was not running a single fixed main event that day.
noticed: The group had already generated competing priorities through earlier decisions.
intervention: Brendon stated that if the town focused on internal problems, an internal problem would arise; if it focused externally, the day's pressure would emerge there instead.
observed_result: The group's own focus became the selector for which prepared pressure moved on-screen.
reusable_judgment: When several legitimate pressures exist, let sustained player attention decide which becomes foreground. Do not force every prepared problem onto the stage at once.
representative_line: “If the town decided to focus on internal problems, an internal problem will arise.”

title: Accommodation stops when the DM starts taking over the player's fun
situation: Players were joking that creating the dating-sim layer was their job, while Brendon was excitedly offering to build more of it.
noticed: His instinct to accommodate could cross from enabling player play into authoring the activity for them.
intervention: Brendon explicitly caught himself and backed off: player agency came first, and he recognized that excitement to accommodate was driving the overreach.
observed_result: The players retained ownership of the emergent dating-sim behavior.
reusable_judgment: Accommodation is not automatically good. If helping starts replacing the player's authorship of the thing they enjoy doing, stop helping and give it back.
representative_line: “right. sorry. player agency. I just get excited trying to accommodate.”

title: Consent boundaries remove some actions from adjudication entirely
situation: PvP conflict emerged in a persistent social game where players could otherwise attempt many actions.
live_evidence: `735726761437823086` (2020-07-23, 🗨 Social / 🙋-out-of-character); `737751675762114581` (2020-07-28, 🚢 Week two, The Tir Na Nog / 🔭-the-observation-deck)
noticed: Treating unwanted PvP as an ordinary contested check would make a safety boundary depend on dice.
intervention: Brendon established that PvP required both players' consent plus a DM, then later applied the rule by refusing even to roll whether one PC could physically stop another when consent had not been granted.
observed_result: The scene proceeded through allowed actions such as following rather than converting the dispute into unauthorized PvP.
reusable_judgment: Some table boundaries are preconditions for adjudication, not modifiers to it. If consent is absent, do not roll to see whether the prohibited interaction happens.
representative_line: “I can't roll to let you stop him. No rolls to stop him, but following is not pvp.”

title: Stop using DM knowledge when it starts choosing a player's story
situation: Brendon was helping reason through who could serve as a witness in a conspiracy/trial thread and realized his DM knowledge could determine another player's involvement.
noticed: His meta-level problem solving was starting to substitute for the player's own decision.
intervention: He stopped the meta-solving, explicitly called it a slippery slope, and put the choice to Web's player instead.
observed_result: The player answered for the character and the channel returned to RP-only mode.
reusable_judgment: Use DM knowledge to maintain the world, not to solve player decisions. When you notice yourself optimizing a player's move from behind the screen, hand the decision back.
representative_line: “lets let web have some player agency I'm meta gaming and its a slippery slope”

title: A cool image is insufficient reason to break established play
situation: A player proposed stacking effects to create a visually spectacular oversized battlefield creature.
noticed: The proposal was exciting but its mechanical implications were unclear and approving it would change precedent.
values: coherence, rules consistency, co-DM alignment, player creativity.
intervention: Brendon expressed enthusiasm for the image but withheld approval pending rules research and Noah's input, weighting the answer toward no because it conflicted with established gameplay.
observed_result: The player accepted the ruling without the cool idea being treated as automatically valid.
reusable_judgment: Reward creativity by seriously considering it, not by automatically approving it. Check implications, precedent, and shared-GM consistency before changing the world to fit the image.
representative_line: “I love the flavor but this is a maybe weighted with a probably no.”

title: When danger lands wrong, fix the telegraph before erasing the consequence
situation: A dangerous sequence caused distress, and players questioned whether the campaign's pressure was becoming harmful or unfair.
noticed: The danger itself fit the campaign's intended pressure, but the fictional signaling had not made the lethality legible enough.
intervention: Brendon kept the legitimate consequence, acknowledged that he should have signaled the danger better through RP, and shifted to transparent discussion of intent.
observed_result: The conversation moved from arguing the outcome toward rebuilding trust and clarifying what kind of pressure the campaign was trying to create.
reusable_judgment: If a dangerous outcome surprises players for the wrong reason, diagnose the information failure. Improve future telegraphing before deciding that the consequence itself must be undone.
representative_line: “I know I should have signaled better how deadly through rp.”

title: The event schedule yields when the table is no longer in a good state to play
situation: After a difficult interpersonal/mental-health discussion, a scheduled hunt was still due to happen.
noticed: Continuing the event would turn the schedule itself into a roadblock and the DM was no longer in a good state to run it.
values: table health, future play, schedule flexibility.
intervention: Brendon offered a mulligan on a painful memory if needed, deferred to the player about their own story, then canceled the night's event rather than forcing the timetable.
observed_result: Players accepted postponement and explicitly suggested returning to the game later.
reusable_judgment: A schedule coordinates play; it does not outrank the humans playing. Cancel or defer content when the current table state would make running it destructive.
representative_line: “I don't want this to become the next road block... I'm canceling tonight's event.”

title: Rewrite campaign architecture when reality destroys the assumptions it depended on
situation: Season 3 was designed around four active faction stories, but two DMs became less active. The remaining structure collapsed into a binary, winner-take-all rivalry that was generating real table drama.
noticed: The original ending architecture no longer produced the intended multi-faction experience because its staffing assumptions had failed.
values: table health, campaign ending, faction meaning, cooperation.
intervention: Brendon and Noah explicitly removed the bipartisan structure and rewrote the Mason and Knight endings so they could function as complementary defense and offense instead of mutually exclusive winners.
observed_result: The finale acquired an in-world reason for the town to cooperate while preserving distinct faction contributions.
reusable_judgment: When an implementation assumption fails, preserve the purpose of the design rather than its original topology. Rewrite the structure that is now producing the wrong experience.
representative_line: “Noah and I are making the choice to eliminate the bipartisan aspect of the game.”

title: Protect the campaign's thematic center when an emergent subsystem begins consuming it
situation: Town politics and the mayoral race had become a dominant emergent activity, while the intended Mason through-line was about building, fellowship, and eventually the Tinker ending.
noticed: The political layer was becoming all-or-nothing and pulling attention away from the relationship/family theme Brendon wanted the season to resolve around.
values: theme, table cohesion, faction identity, emergent play.
intervention: Brendon articulated that the season's focus was bringing people together as friends and family, moved the Mason symbolism toward the rebuilt pub rather than governance, and resisted blame-focused politics in the final week.
observed_result: The Mason story was reframed around rebuilding/community while final-week messaging emphasized coming back together.
reusable_judgment: Let emergent systems grow while they enrich the campaign. Redirect them when they begin cannibalizing the story's central concern or damaging table cohesion.
representative_line: “our story was meant to be about something other than governance.”

title: Correct a broken rule prospectively while honoring outcomes already earned under it
situation: A resurrection house rule proved too strong in actual play.
prep_evidence: No direct pre-session rule located; runtime evidence only.
noticed: The rule was creating a balance problem that could not remain in the campaign as written.
values: game balance, fairness, trust in rulings.
intervention: Brendon publicly called the rule a genuine mistake, nerfed it going forward, and explicitly let that night's resurrections stand.
observed_result: The system changed without retroactively invalidating player outcomes that had been legal when they occurred.
reusable_judgment: When a house rule fails in live play, fix it. Prefer prospective correction and preserve already-resolved outcomes unless the existing result is itself intolerable.
representative_line: “Tonight's rez's still stand but the once per day rule can't stay in the game.”

title: Downgrade encounter mode when turnout cannot support the intended challenge
situation: A dangerous tree encounter was planned, but the available player count was uncertain.
noticed: The encounter's combat form depended on enough participants to make the risk and pacing work.
intervention: Brendon declared in advance that insufficient turnout would convert the event to exploration only and that the fight could be skipped until later.
observed_result: The world remained explorable without forcing an understrength party into the combat merely because the encounter was scheduled.
reusable_judgment: Treat encounter mode as conditional on the table state. If the group cannot support the intended challenge, preserve exploration/information and defer the fight.
representative_line: “If there aren't enough players to to take on the tree it will be exploration only.”
